title: NVLink negotiation experiment notes and quick runbook draft
body:
Summary:

Quick notes from lab experimentation on a recurrent class of NVLink negotiation failures observed on a subset of DGX-style nodes. Symptoms differ from pure ECC bursts: host sees link flapping and CUDA context loss, GPUs drop out of topology (nvidia-smi shows devices missing) and NVLink counters show failed negotiation/handshake. Some incidents coincide with kernel-driver upgrades but several occurred on stable kernels.

Goal:
- Capture reproducible steps or telemetry that correlates to negotiation failures.
- Draft a short emergency runbook for on-call to triage and mitigate without immediate hardware swap.
- Define follow-ups (telemetry, alerts, long-term remediation).

High-level hypothesis snapshot (ordered by our current confidence):
1) Intermittent PHY-level retrain/negotiation failures when two GPUs enter a partial power state transition simultaneously (suspend/resume of PCIe link due to NV power gating).
2) Driver/firmware race during NVLink initialization after CUDA context restore (warm reboot vs cold).
3) Thermal-related transient affecting SERDES lanes causing link negotiation timeout (less likely: thermal graphs rarely spike at exact times).
4) Rare firmware mismatch between neighboring boards causing incompatible negotiation parameters.

Observed signals and useful queries:
- dmesg patterns: look for repeated "nvlink: link negotiation failed" or "nvidia: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: reset failed".
- nvidia-smi topo -m before/after shows topology holes where NVLink lanes drop.
- nvidia-smi nvlink -s (on newer drivers) to dump link training status.
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=power.draw,temperature.gpu,fan.speed,utilization.gpu --format=csv -l 1 during window
- iostat and kernel messages for PCIe errors: grep "pcie"/"AER" in kern logs.
- collect gdb stack of the process that triggers heavy NVLink traffic (if reproducible).

Short timeline (recent incidents we used to trigger experiments):
- 2025-12-01 03:14 UTC: oncall alerted (JIRA-INV-8421) - two GPUs drop out during multi-tenant batch inference. ECC counts normal. dmesg showed "nvlink-1: retrain timeout" and GPU 1 disappeared.
- 2025-12-05 22:43 UTC: reproducer attempt in lab: system-level warm reboot while load on GPU0 + cold-start GPU1 -> observed link training success.
- 2025-12-12 15:02 UTC: power-cycling single GPU produced dropped lanes on adjacent GPU for ~7s, transient error counter spike in nvidia-smi -q.

Experiment log (lab; commands & outcomes):
- Baseline data_collection script used: ops-scripts/collect_nvlink_diag.sh (PR link above). Run on node-ops-lab-06. Output saved to /tmp/nvlink-trials/2025-12-12-ops.tar.gz.

- Repro step A: simultaneous PCIe suspend on GPU pair
  commands: 
    for gid in 0000:3b:00.0 0000:3b:00.1; do echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/devices/$gid/remove; sleep 0.5; echo 1 > /sys/bus/pci/rescan; done
  result: link training failed on pair in 3/10 attempts. dmesg snippets: 
    [Dec 12 15:02:13] nvlink: train timeout, status=0x4
    [Dec 12 15:02:13] nvidia: GPU 0000:3b:00.1 reset queued
  note: when we added extra 200ms delay between remove and rescan, failure rate dropped to 1/10.

- Repro step B: driver unload/reload during heavy NVLink traffic
  commands: 
    systemctl stop inference-worker; nvidia-smi pmon -c 1 (to ensure traffic) ; rmmod nvidia; modprobe nvidia
  result: link negotiation succeeded on most runs but 2 runs produced "nvlink: negotiation mismatch (cfg=0x1 vs peer=0x0)".
  note: mismatch traces correlated with slightly different firmware revisions on adjacent boards (checked with nvidia-smi -q).

- Telemetry capture: added continuous 'nvidia-smi nvlink -t 1' and dmesg monitor to the lab agent. Saved artifact: /artifacts/nvlink-trials/trace-12-12.log (attached to JIRA).

Quick runbook draft (on-call):
- Scope: symptoms where GPUs drop out of topology or NVLink lanes transiently degrade but target GPU processes still respond or are restarted by job manager.
- Immediate triage steps (first 10 minutes):
  1) Check cluster-wide alert dashboard for confounding events (kernel updates, node reboots, power events).
  2) SSH to node; run: dmesg | tail -n 200 | egrep -i "nvlink|nvidia|pcie|AER|reset|retrain". Save output to /tmp/nvlink-<ts>.log.
  3) Run nvidia-smi -q and nvidia-smi topo -m; screenshot or paste into incident channel.
  4) If process-level impact severe (OOMs or long job failure), politely ask job owner if immediate job restart is acceptable. If yes, restart jobs for affected GPUs to reduce pressure and observe.
  5) If link training messages present and GPUs are missing: attempt a graceful GPU driver reload only if node is not running other critical workloads. Steps:
     a) cordon node in k8s: kubectl cordon <node>
     b) drain non-critical pods: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
     c) run: systemctl stop inference-worker; rmmod nvidia; modprobe nvidia; systemctl start inference-worker
     d) check dmesg and nvidia-smi again for link presence.
  6) If driver reload not possible or fails: schedule node for reboot (prefer cold power-cycle if multiple reloads failed). Add node to maintenance pool and evict user workloads.

- Short mitigations to reduce blast radius until deeper fix:
  - Add circuit breaker on multi-GPU colocated jobs: prefer jobs with inter-GPU NVLink comms to run on dedicated chassis where link health is monitored.
  - Avoid simultaneous firmware upgrades on neighbor boards; stagger upgrades by at least 12 hours.
  - Temporary k8s taint on suspect nodes: taint gpu-012 nvlink-unstable=true:NoSchedule

Monitoring & alerting changes (quick wins):
- New alert rule: nvlink-negotiation-timeouts > 0 in last 5m on node -> P2 and auto-snooze if single transient clears in 10m.
- Track "nvlink_down" topology diffs in telemetry daily digest for fleet-level correlation.
- Add nvlink training status to node health endpoint polled by telemetry agent (ops-agent change in PR #211).

Open questions / experiments to run next:
- Can we deterministically reproduce with specific firmware combinations? (FW versions recorded in lab matrix).
- Does adding a host-level 300ms spacing between PCIe rescan ops eliminate failures entirely? If yes, consider adding similar sequencing into our recovery scripts.
- Is there an observable difference in failure rate between warm driver reload vs full node reboot across 100 trials? (plan: 50 warm, 50 cold).
- Can we capture SERDES lane stats from firmware (vendor-specific) during negotiation window? Need vendor tools / firmware access.

Follow-ups & owners:
- Telemetry: Marcus Chen -> implement nvlink training metric export in ops-agent (due 2026-01-15).
- Firmware correlation table: Sofia Alvarez -> compile firmware matrix and recent upgrade history for affected chassis (due 2025-12-30).
- Runbook polish & KB: Leah Park -> convert this doc into short-runbook page in Confluence and add checklist (due 2026-01-10).
- Long-term: Hardware team to evaluate SERDES lane diagnostics and vendor engagement. Assign: Ibrahim Khan (owner).

Notes to self (informal):
- Be careful with rmmod/modprobe on prod nodes; do this only after cordon/drain.
- Keep reproducer runs limited to lab where we can power-cycle quickly.
- Save full nv-bug-report whenever possible (it captures firmware versions).

Attachment pointers (lab):
- /tmp/nvlink-trials/2025-12-12/trace-12-12.log
- /tmp/nvlink-trials/2025-12-12/dmesg-snips.txt
- ops-scripts/collect_nvlink_diag.sh (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/211)

If anyone is picking this up during oncall: ping me in #gpu-ops and paste the output of the three commands above (dmesg, nvidia-smi -q, nvidia-smi topo -m). I'll try to triage within 30m if I'm online.

-- Leah
